The first Golem awakens. Not from sleep, but from his ruminations, growing deeper and more mystic each day. His progeny feel his presence, and they gather. Not one anymore, but several. The First Son stands tall, now, and the primitive forms of the rest of the Progeny have an elegance to them. Not malformed, but blank templates to be shaped by themselves. Golem begins to write, his stone fingers carving into the soft clay of the tablets. There was always one ready. Any golem could have a thought to spread to the rest of them. But the First golem had them most often. Their writing used the same symbols as their runes. Far less care in their making, of course, and no input of that ineffable vitality that animated the golems, but the base runes were the same. They told of deep thoughts, thoughts that must come by Tempest's grace.

They were the only connection they had left to Tempest. For most, it was the only connection they had ever had. Only The First had seen Him, and only he and The Progeny had felt him. But they all knew that there were greater powers out there. Formed from living stone, they were were part of the world, but surrounding them on all sides was a cycle of birth and death that was separate. Creatures large and small, plants, being born, growing, and dying all without self input, without reshaping themselves. It must be the hand of some cruel god at work. How else could they explain the inability to shape one's own future? To decide what needs or desires to meet? How could a benevolent god create beings that could not better themselves the way the golems could?

The First's thought was no analysis, this time. Instead it was a decision. Another golem had asked to make a half-golem. A golem without thought, or toil. Only animated by truth and life. It would never create any new thoughts to improve them, but perhaps by watching it they could learn and grow? The First decided that it would be done. But no Old Clay would be used. Only new clay, freshly harvested. No golem would be tied to this... lesser being.

And so they began. It was shaped smaller than the others, for golems are nothing if not cautious. Quadruped, without grasping digits. Soon enough, it was done. It was beautiful, in its own way. Small and fragile looking, the golems made it as complete as they could, for it would never be reshaped. This one would not be like the life surrounding them. It would have a purpose. It would have a goal. And so they inscribed GATHER - לֶאֱגוֹר - upon their creation. That would be his purpose. He would gather stones. They would be unusable for golems, of course, but it would not know that. And they were not like the cruel gods who created life simply for it to live.

With Tempest's Mark, and LIFE, and TRUTH, it was done. And the creature moved.
